name: TP-Link Easy Smart switch
author: Netlens
description: Reads a TP-Link Easy Smart switch (TL-SG105E, TL-SG108E, TL-SG1016PE, TL-SG1024DE and relatives) from its web page: the switch as a network node with the state, speed and packet counters of every port. Netlens shows them on the switch's device page and logs an event when a port goes down or comes back. These switches have no SNMP and no MAC address table, so the devices behind a port cannot be listed. Read-only: it only reads two status pages and logs out again.

info.title: Good to know before you switch it on
info.text: Easy Smart switches speak plain HTTP and, once someone has logged in, treat every request from that same IP address as logged in (CVE-2017-17746). Netlens logs out after each read, but run it from a machine that you trust (the Netlens container's host) and keep the switch on a trusted network. Use the switch's own login (the default user is admin); only 16 sessions fit, so close any open browser tab on the switch when a read fails with 'sessions full'. The password can be at most 16 characters long (the switch's limit).
